name: Broccoli
description: A cool-season crop that produces a large central head, followed by smaller side shoots.
tips: Transplant into the garden before the weather gets too hot. Heat can cause it to bolt. Harvest the main head before the flowers open.

careTasks.name: Begin hardening off seedlings
careTasks.description: Gradually expose seedlings to outdoor conditions over a week to prevent shock.

careTasks.name: Fertilize 3 weeks after transplanting
careTasks.description: Feed your Broccoli with a balanced fertilizer to support healthy growth and fruit development.

careTasks.name: Check for cabbage worms
careTasks.description: Inspect leaves for small green caterpillars and their droppings. Remove them by hand or use an appropriate organic pesticide.

careTasks.name: Harvest main head when buds are tight
careTasks.description: Harvest your Broccoli when they reach a mature size and color. Regular harvesting can encourage more production.

careTasks.name: Continue harvesting side shoots
careTasks.description: Harvest your Broccoli when they reach a mature size and color. Regular harvesting can encourage more production.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water your Broccoli consistently. Provide about 1-2 inches of water per week, adjusting for rainfall.

name: Cabbage
description: A cool-season crop that forms dense heads. Can split if growth is too rapid.
tips: Harvest when heads are firm and solid. Cut at base leaving roots to potentially produce small secondary heads.

careTasks.name: Begin hardening off seedlings
careTasks.description: Gradually expose seedlings to outdoor conditions over a week to prevent shock.

careTasks.name: Check for cabbage worms
careTasks.description: Inspect leaves for small green caterpillars and their droppings. Remove them by hand or use an appropriate organic pesticide.

careTasks.name: Check heads for firmness
careTasks.description: Perform the task: Check heads for firmness.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water your Cabbage consistently. Provide about 1-2 inches of water per week, adjusting for rainfall.

name: Cauliflower
description: A cool-season crop that requires steady temperatures. More finicky than cabbage.
tips: Blanch heads by tying leaves over them when heads are 2-3 inches across to keep them white.

careTasks.name: Begin hardening off seedlings
careTasks.description: Gradually expose seedlings to outdoor conditions over a week to prevent shock.

careTasks.name: Tie leaves over developing heads to blanch
careTasks.description: Perform the task: Tie leaves over developing heads to blanch.

careTasks.name: Check for harvest readiness
careTasks.description: Harvest your Cauliflower when they reach a mature size and color. Regular harvesting can encourage more production.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water your Cauliflower consistently. Provide about 1-2 inches of water per week, adjusting for rainfall.

name: Brussels Sprouts
description: A long-season cool-weather crop. Sprouts form along the tall stem.
tips: Remove lower leaves as sprouts develop. Harvest from bottom up when sprouts are firm and 1-2 inches across.

careTasks.name: Begin hardening off seedlings

careTasks.name: Remove lower leaves to expose developing sprouts

careTasks.description: Harvest your Brussels Sprouts when they reach a mature size and color. Regular harvesting can encourage more production.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water your Brussels Sprouts consistently. Provide about 1-2 inches of water per week, adjusting for rainfall.

name: Leeks
description: A long-season cool-weather crop related to onions, grown for thick white stems.
tips: Hill soil around stems to blanch them white. Very cold hardy and can be harvested into winter.

name: Asparagus
description: A perennial vegetable that takes 2-3 years to establish but produces for decades.
tips: Do not harvest in the first year. Allow ferns to grow to build root system. Harvest spears for 6-8 weeks in spring.

tips: Harvest buds before they open into flowers. Cut main bud first to encourage side shoots.
